rationale: Blocking: USER-scope ms_teams settings are never rejected (POST/PUT /v1/settings/user has no MS_TEAMS branch, and the validator's own setting_type!=PROJECT guard is unreachable since project_settings.py hardcodes PROJECT), which fails the spec's required USER-scope rejection criterion; a code-quality standard (Optional[X] vs X | None) is violated; and assistant_ids validation is under-strict (accepts empty list, drops extra duplicate-keyed entries, never dedupes ids). 1 deferred: update_project_setting validates ms_teams singleton/ownership against the request body's project_name rather than the target setting's actual project, but this mirrors the pre-existing, unchanged check_alias_unique pattern shared by every credential type, so fixing it here alone is out of this story's scope. 7 findings dismissed as noise after verifying against source: the reported enum-case mismatch (model uses 'ms_teams', migration uses 'MS_TEAMS') is not a bug — SQLAlchemy Enum columns store the member name, and every prior credential-type migration (e.g. GOOGLE_OAUTH) follows the identical name-based pattern; the matching downgrade()-delete-mismatch claim is the same false premise; check_ms_teams_singleton's get_by_fields(...).id usage exactly mirrors the pre-existing check_alias_unique/check_webhook_id_unique pattern in the same file; the claimed unused CredentialTypes import does not exist in settings_request_validator.py; the check-then-create singleton race is an explicit trade-off named by the original task itself ('app-level singleton'); an uncaught non-ValueError from check_ms_teams_singleton mirrors existing handling elsewhere; and an empty/None project_name still fails safely via the assistant-ownership check.

findings.title: USER-scope ms_teams settings bypass all validation
findings.problem: create_user_setting/update_user_setting (lines 127-148, 166-195) have no CredentialTypes.MS_TEAMS branch and never call validate_ms_teams_request. Separately, validate_ms_teams_request's own 'setting_type != SettingType.PROJECT' rejection (settings_request_validator.py:277-283) is dead code: it is only ever invoked from project_settings.py, which hardcodes setting_type=SettingType.PROJECT regardless of the request body, so that guard can never fire from any real HTTP request.
findings.impact: A POST or PUT to /v1/settings/user with credential_type=ms_teams is persisted as a USER-scoped row with none of the required checks applied (no PROJECT-scope enforcement, no assistant_ids validation, no per-project singleton check), directly contradicting the explicit spec requirement that ms_teams stay project-scope only.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit rejection for credential_type == CredentialTypes.MS_TEAMS in create_user_setting/update_user_setting (mirroring the pattern used for SCHEDULER/LITE_LLM/GIT/WEBHOOK), or otherwise make the USER-scope rejection reachable from a real route; add a test exercising /v1/settings/user with credential_type=ms_teams.

findings.title: New Optional[X] import breaks module's X | None style
findings.problem: The new validate_ms_teams_request signature types setting_id as 'Optional[str] = None' and adds a fresh 'from typing import Optional' import, even though the module already uses 'from __future__ import annotations' and the preferred 'IndexInfo | None' union style elsewhere.
findings.impact: Violates the documented code-quality standard for new code and is inconsistent with this module's own already-established pattern.
findings.recommendation: Type the parameter as 'setting_id: str | None = None' and drop the new Optional import from the typing import line.

findings.title: assistant_ids extraction under-validates its input
findings.problem: The 'assistant_ids' credential_values entry is extracted with next((cv for cv in request.credential_values if cv.key == "assistant_ids"), None) and only checked for presence and list-type: an empty list passes through, any additional entries also keyed 'assistant_ids' beyond the first are silently discarded rather than rejected, and duplicate ids within the list are neither deduplicated nor rejected.
findings.impact: Allows creating/updating an ms_teams integration with zero linked assistants (defeating its purpose), silently drops a second assistant_ids payload without validating it, and allows the same assistant id to be stored multiple times against one integration.
findings.recommendation: Reject an empty or missing assistant_ids list; reject (or explicitly merge-and-validate) more than one credential_values entry keyed 'assistant_ids'; reject or deduplicate repeated ids within the list before running the per-id ownership check.
